T0603.title: Protocol Crawler
T0603.definition: A crawler that directly constructs requests over HTTP or custom protocols, bypassing browser rendering — contrasted with headless-browser crawlers and real-device crawlers — and a primary target of anti-scraping defense.
T0603.description: A protocol crawler is a crawler type that does not rely on a browser rendering environment, but directly constructs requests over HTTP or custom protocols to obtain data. Compared with headless-browser crawlers (AT0022, which rely on a browser kernel to render pages and execute JS) and real-device crawlers (which rely on real-device operations), protocol crawlers are lightweight, efficient, and highly concurrent, but must self-handle front-end defenses such as API signatures, parameter encryption, and JS-involved computation, often working with packet-capture tools (AT0014) to reverse-engineer interface protocols. Because protocol crawlers do not carry real-browser characteristics, their TLS/HTTP fingerprints, JS execution environment, and behavioral features all differ from a real browser, making them a primary target of TLS/HTTP fingerprinting (A0038-003) and abnormal-environment detection (A0010). In anti-scraping practice, although protocol crawlers, headless-browser crawlers, real-device crawlers, and crowd-sourced human crawlers differ in technical form, there is no need to strictly distinguish them from a defense perspective — common high-coverage problems should be addressed first.
T0603.usageExample: Risk control detected a large volume of protocol crawlers directly calling API endpoints to scrape product-detail data via TLS fingerprinting, triggering cloud anti-scraping to block them.
